page: Amazon Web Services r8id.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and INT8 operations.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks falling into the bottom 10 percent and bottom 25 percent respectively, reflecting the single physical core constraint. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is relatively weak, though Passmark memory scores remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8id.large offers a high-density memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed DDR5 memory alongside local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suited for single-threaded data processing, lightweight database operations, caching layers, and applications requiring fast local temporary storage.
